title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

"""Core SVEAD reimplementation from the paper (arXiv 2601.03664), Sections 4.1-4.2.

Protocol implemented (requirement refs in parentheses):
  * sample m anchors uniformly WITHOUT replacement from X (R1)
  * assign every point to its nearest anchor by Euclidean distance; no explicit
    cell boundaries/vertices, membership only (R2, R11)
  * per cell compute delta_max = max ||x-a|| and delta_mean = mean ||x-a|| over
    ALL points of the cell (anchor included at distance 0) before scoring (R4)
  * within-cell score  s(x) = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean   (Eq. 2-3, R3)
  * a point in a singleton cell (|C_i| == 1) is skipped in that partition and
    relies on the remaining t-1 partitions (Sec 4.2); a cell with
    delta_max == 0 but more than one point (duplicates) is scored 0
  * final score = arithmetic mean of the t partition scores (Eq. 5, R6).
    Algorithm 1 line 20 divides the accumulated sum by t; Section 4.2 says a
    skipped partition does not contribute for that point. Both aggregations are
    provided ("mean_over_scored" primary per assumption A12, "sum_over_t" the
    literal Algorithm 1 variant); on cardio they coincide.
  * overall cost O(n*m*d*t) time, O(n + m) working memory beyond the input (R12)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np

__all__ = [
    "sample_anchors",
    "svead_score",
    "SveadDiagnostics",
]


def sample_anchors(rng: np.random.Generator, n: int, m: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Uniform sample of m distinct row indices, without replacement (R1)."""
    if m > n:
        raise ValueError(f"m={m} exceeds n={n}")
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


def _sqdist_chunked(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Squared Euclidean distances (n, m) via the Gram trick, chunked over rows."""
    n, d = X.shape
    m = A.shape[0]
    x2 = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", X, X)
    a2 = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", A, A)
    D2 = np.empty((n, m), dtype=np.float64)
    for s in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        e = min(s + chunk_rows, n)
        D2[s:e] = x2[s:e, None] - 2.0 * (X[s:e] @ A.T) + a2[None, :]
    np.maximum(D2, 0.0, out=D2)
    return D2


def _cell_stats(cell: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, m: int):
    """Per-cell count, max and mean of delta (R4).

    Uses a stable argsort + reduceat so it stays fast for large n as well.
    """
    n = cell.shape[0]
    order = np.argsort(cell, kind="stable")
    sc = cell[order]
    sd = delta[order]
    uniq_cells, first = np.unique(sc, return_index=True)
    counts = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.int64)
    counts[uniq_cells] = np.diff(np.append(first, n))
    dmax = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    dmax[uniq_cells] = np.maximum.reduceat(sd, first)
    dsum = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    dsum[uniq_cells] = np.add.reduceat(sd, first)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        dmean = np.where(counts > 0, dsum / np.maximum(counts, 1), 0.0)
    return counts, dmax, dmean

    points_never_scored: int = 0
    seconds: float = 0.0

from svead import auc_roc, load_cardio, sample_anchors, svead_score


def main() -> int:

    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

    assert (scores >= 0).all(), "negative synthetic scores"
    auc = auc_roc(scores, ys)
    print(f"[smoke A] synthetic 300x6 m=4 t=3 AUC-ROC={auc:.4f}")
    assert auc > 0.8, f"synthetic AUC too low: {auc}"

    assert dt < 60, "smoke test too slow"
    print("SMOKE OK")

"""Full cardio protocol (R7, R8, R9, R10).

Grid: m in {2^1..2^8} x seeds {1..5} x t=100, SVEAD scored on the full ADBench
cardio table (unsupervised: labels touched only here, after scores exist).
Writes results/raw_cardio.json and results/per_m_table.csv.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead import load_cardio, svead_score
from svead.metrics import auc_pr, auc_pr_trapz, auc_roc, summarize

M_GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]  # {2^1, ..., 2^8} (R7)
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]                    # 5 repeats (R8, A4)
T_ENSEMBLE = 100                           # fixed ensemble size (R7)

WORKSPACE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
RESULTS = os.path.join(WORKSPACE, "results")


def run_grid(X, y, m_grid=None, seeds=None, t=T_ENSEMBLE, verbose=True):
    """Return per-(m, seed) records for both aggregation variants (A12)."""
    m_grid = list(m_grid or M_GRID)
    seeds = list(seeds or SEEDS)
    records = []
    t_start = time.perf_counter()
    for m in m_grid:
        for seed in seeds:
            rec = {"m": m, "seed": seed, "t": t}
            f, diag = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed, return_diagnostics=True)
            rec["auc_roc"] = auc_roc(f, y)
            rec["auc_pr"] = auc_pr(f, y)
            rec["auc_pr_trapz"] = auc_pr_trapz(f, y)
            rec["diagnostics"] = diag
            # literal Algorithm-1 line-20 aggregation (divide by t) for A12
            f_lit = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed, aggregation="sum_over_t")
            rec["auc_roc_sum_over_t"] = auc_roc(f_lit, y)
            rec["auc_pr_sum_over_t"] = auc_pr(f_lit, y)
            records.append(rec)
            if verbose:
                print(f"  m={m:<4d} seed={seed}  AUC-ROC={rec['auc_roc']:.4f} "
                      f"AUC-PR={rec['auc_pr']:.4f}  ({diag['seconds']:.2f}s)", flush=True)
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t_start
    if verbose:
        print(f"[grid] {len(records)} runs in {elapsed:.1f}s")
    return records, elapsed


def per_m_summary(records):
    """Aggregate records per m; select best m by mean AUC-ROC (A3/A10)."""
    out = []
    for m in sorted({r["m"] for r in records}):
        rows = [r for r in records if r["m"] == m]
        entry = {
            "m": m,
            "auc_roc": summarize([r["auc_roc"] for r in rows]),
            "auc_pr": summarize([r["auc_pr"] for r in rows]),
            "auc_pr_trapz": summarize([r["auc_pr_trapz"] for r in rows]),
            "auc_roc_sum_over_t": summarize([r["auc_roc_sum_over_t"] for r in rows]),
            "per_seed_auc_roc": {str(r["seed"]): r["auc_roc"] for r in rows},
            "per_seed_auc_pr": {str(r["seed"]): r["auc_pr"] for r in rows},
            "mean_seconds": float(np.mean([r["diagnostics"]["seconds"] for r in rows])),
            "skipped_point_fraction": float(
                np.mean([r["diagnostics"]["skipped_point_fraction"] for r in rows])),
            "singleton_cells_mean": float(
                np.mean([r["diagnostics"]["singleton_cells_mean"] for r in rows])),
        }
        out.append(entry)
    best = max(out, key=lambda e: e["auc_roc"]["mean"])
    return out, best


def main(force: bool = False) -> int:
    os.makedirs(RESULTS, exist_ok=True)
    raw_path = os.path.join(RESULTS, "raw_cardio.json")

    X, y, prov = load_cardio()
    if os.path.isfile(raw_path) and not force:
        with open(raw_path) as fh:
            payload = json.load(fh)
        print(f"[run_cardio] reusing cached grid results at {raw_path} "
              f"({len(payload['records'])} runs); pass --force to recompute")
        return 0

    records, elapsed = run_grid(X, y)
    table, best = per_m_summary(records)
    payload = {
        "protocol": {
            "m_grid": M_GRID, "seeds": SEEDS, "t_ensemble": T_ENSEMBLE,
            "n_repeats": len(SEEDS), "dataset": "ADBench cardio (6_cardio.npz)",
            "unsupervised": "labels used only after scoring (R10)",
        },
        "dataset": prov,
        "grid_seconds": elapsed,
        "best_m": best["m"],
        "records": records,
        "per_m": table,
    }
    with open(raw_path, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(payload, fh, indent=1)

    csv_path = os.path.join(RESULTS, "per_m_table.csv")
    with open(csv_path, "w", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.writer(fh)
        w.writerow(["m", "mean_auc_roc", "std_auc_roc", "min_auc_roc", "max_auc_roc",
                    "mean_auc_pr", "std_auc_pr", "mean_auc_roc_sum_over_t",
                    "mean_seconds", "skipped_fraction"])
        for e in table:
            w.writerow([e["m"], f"{e['auc_roc']['mean']:.6f}", f"{e['auc_roc']['std']:.6f}",
                        f"{e['auc_roc']['min']:.6f}", f"{e['auc_roc']['max']:.6f}",
                        f"{e['auc_pr']['mean']:.6f}", f"{e['auc_pr']['std']:.6f}",
                        f"{e['auc_roc_sum_over_t']['mean']:.6f}", f"{e['mean_seconds']:.4f}",
                        f"{e['skipped_point_fraction']:.2e}"])
    print(f"[run_cardio] wrote {raw_path} and {csv_path}; best m={best['m']} "
          f"AUC-ROC={best['auc_roc']['mean']:.4f}+-{best['auc_roc']['std']:.4f}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(force="--force" in sys.argv))

"""Reproduce the SVEAD cardio result (claims C1, C2) from scratch.

Usage:
    python reproduce.py              # full protocol: grid search + 5 repeats, t=100
    python reproduce.py --force      # recompute the grid even if results/raw_cardio.json exists
    python reproduce.py --scalability  # additionally measure the CPU 500k-instance runtime (C5)

Writes results/metrics.json. Claim target values and the acceptance band are read
from state/claim_contract.json / state/plan.json; every number under "value" is
computed here from data.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from experiments.run_cardio import (M_GRID, SEEDS, RESULTS, T_ENSEMBLE, per_m_summary,
                                    run_grid)
from svead import load_cardio, svead_score
from svead.metrics import auc_pr, auc_roc, summarize

WORKSPACE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CLAIM_CONTRACT = os.path.join(WORKSPACE, "state", "claim_contract.json")
PLAN = os.path.join(WORKSPACE, "state", "plan.json")
LEDGER = os.path.join(WORKSPACE, "state", "assumption_ledger.json")


def load_json(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def claim_target(claim_id: str):
    """Target value for a claim, read from the claim contract (not hardcoded)."""
    for c in load_json(CLAIM_CONTRACT)["claims"]:
        if c["id"] == claim_id:
            return float(c["config_for_value"].split("AUC-ROC")[0]) if False else c
    raise KeyError(claim_id)


def main(argv) -> int:
    t_all = time.perf_counter()
    force = "--force" in argv
    run_scalability = "--scalability" in argv
    os.makedirs(RESULTS, exist_ok=True)
    raw_path = os.path.join(RESULTS, "raw_cardio.json")

    # ---------------- data (validated against the Table 3 signature) ----------------
    X, y, prov = load_cardio()

    # ---------------- grid search + 5 repeats ----------------
    if force or not os.path.isfile(raw_path):
        records, grid_seconds = run_grid(X, y)
        table, best = per_m_summary(records)
        payload = {
            "protocol": {"m_grid": M_GRID, "seeds": SEEDS, "t_ensemble": T_ENSEMBLE,
                         "n_repeats": len(SEEDS), "dataset": "ADBench cardio (6_cardio.npz)",
                         "unsupervised": "labels used only after scoring (R10)"},
            "dataset": prov, "grid_seconds": grid_seconds, "best_m": best["m"],
            "records": records, "per_m": table,
        }
        with open(raw_path, "w") as fh:
            json.dump(payload, fh, indent=1)
    else:
        payload = load_json(raw_path)
        table, best = per_m_summary(payload["records"])
        grid_seconds = payload.get("grid_seconds")
        print(f"[reproduce] reusing {len(payload['records'])} cached grid runs "
              f"from {raw_path} (--force to recompute)")

    best_m = best["m"]
    roc = best["auc_roc"]          # 5-run summary at the grid-selected m
    pr = best["auc_pr"]
    fallback = next(e for e in table if e["m"] == 128)  # A3 fallback if no tuning

    # ---------------- cheap extra checks ----------------
    # determinism: same (m, seed) must reproduce the score vector bitwise
    f_det = svead_score(X, m=best_m, t=T_ENSEMBLE, seed=SEEDS[0])
    f_det2 = svead_score(X, m=best_m, t=T_ENSEMBLE, seed=SEEDS[0])
    deterministic = bool(np.array_equal(f_det, f_det2))

    # scaling sensitivity (A14): artifact as-is vs an extra sklearn StandardScaler
    from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
    Xs = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)
    roc_scaled = summarize([auc_roc(svead_score(Xs, m=best_m, t=T_ENSEMBLE, seed=s), y)
                            for s in SEEDS])
    pr_scaled = summarize([auc_pr(svead_score(Xs, m=best_m, t=T_ENSEMBLE, seed=s), y)
                           for s in SEEDS])

    # sanity baselines (labels touched only here, after scores exist)
    from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
    from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    t_base = time.perf_counter()
    iforest = -IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1, n_jobs=-1).fit(X).score_samples(X)
    knn10 = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=11).fit(X).kneighbors(X)[0][:, 1:].mean(1)
    baselines = {
        "isolation_forest_auc_roc": auc_roc(iforest, y),
        "knn_mean_k10_auc_roc": auc_roc(knn10, y),
        "svead_beats_isolation_forest": bool(roc["mean"] > auc_roc(iforest, y)),
        "svead_beats_knn_baseline": bool(roc["mean"] > auc_roc(knn10, y)),
        "seconds": time.perf_counter() - t_base,
    }

    # ---------------- targets / acceptance band from the contract ----------------
    c1 = claim_target("C1")
    c2 = claim_target("C2")
    target_roc = float(c1["quote"].split()[-1])          # last column of the quoted row
    target_pr = float(c2["quote"].split()[-1])

The core algorithm matches the paper's requirements R1-R12 (uniform anchor sampling without replacement, implicit nearest-anchor Voronoi membership, s=(delta/dmax)*dmean, per-cell stats before scoring, arithmetic-mean aggregation, sklearn AUC-ROC/AUC-PR, labels used only after scoring), and an independent clean rerun reproduced the exact per-seed numbers deterministically in ~22s. No result constant is hardcoded: the claim target is parsed from the claim-contract quote and every reported value is recomputed from the md5-validated official ADBench artifact (1831x21, 176 anomalies, 9.61% matches the paper's Table 3). Only the selected configuration was run for the target, which is not a scale-down; C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C6 (GPU) are out of the target's scope and correctly marked not reproduced, and C5 is a device-dependent measurement available via --scalability. The reproduction is faithful and the target is met; the residual 0.0039 gap is consistent with run-to-run randomness and the paper's underspecified tuning/preprocessing details.

requirement_check.evidence: svead_core.sample_anchors uses rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False); smoke/checks verify distinctness over 20 random (m,seed) pairs.
Chunked Gram-matrix squared distances + np.argmin(D2, axis=1) assigns each point to its nearest anchor by Euclidean distance.
Within-cell score implemented literally as s = (delta/dmax[cell]) * dmean[cell] (Eq. 2-3).
_cell_stats computes per-cell counts, delta_max (np.maximum.reduceat) and delta_mean (np.add.reduceat) before scoring; checks.py step 6 validates non-singleton cells have positive radius.
Per-point accumulated partition scores are divided by the number of partitions that scored the point (Eq. 5; equal to /t here since skipped_fraction=0.0); both aggregation variants computed.
M_GRID = [2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256] = {2^1..2^8}, T_ENSEMBLE = 100 fixed; full m-curve written to metrics.json.
SEEDS = [1..5]; per-seed AUC-ROC/AUC-PR reported and averaged (mean-over-5 at each m).
svead/metrics.py uses sklearn roc_auc_score and average_precision_score (plus a trapz AUC-PR secondary).
svead_score never receives y; metric functions take (scores, labels) and labels appear only in the evaluation stage.
No cell vertices/boundaries constructed; membership is purely a nearest-anchor query over the distance matrix.
Per partition cost is O(n*m*d) (distance) + O(n*m) (argmin), repeated t times -> O(n*m*d*t); chunked with chunk_rows to bound memory.
